name: Hungersome Wolf

items.name: Better to See You With
items.text: The wolf's keen sense of sight can see through both mundane and magical hindrances when they have their sights set on their prey. The wolf ignores their prey's concealment if they're visible. If their prey is invisible, the wolf treats their invisibility as concealment instead.

items.name: Run If You Can
items.text:
Trigger A creature within reach of the wolf's jaws attempts to move out of reach

---
Effect The hungersome wolf attempts a jaws Strike against the triggering creature. On a hit, they disrupt the triggering creature's move action.

items.name: Stalk Prey
items.text:
The hungersome wolf designates a single sapient creature they can smell and hear as their prey. The hungersome wolf gains a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to seek their prey and Survival checks to track their prey. The wolf gains an additional reaction each round they can use only for Run If You Can against their prey.

If the wolf uses Stalk Prey again, any creature they'd designated as their prey is no longer their prey.

items.name: You Are What You Eat
items.text: This functions as Change Shape, except the hungersome wolf must transform into the last creature they Swallowed Whole. This doesn't change their Speed or their attack and damage bonuses, but it might change the damage type their Strikes deal (typically to bludgeoning). The transformation lasts until the hungersome wolf takes 20 or more damage from a single ability, attack, or spell.

text:
A hungersome wolf is a fearsome beast who stalks the forests of the First World, following after their prey with silent steps and unending patience. They're known to choose a target and bide their time, finding out the target's usual routes and routines, eventually identifying the perfect time and place to strike. When the moment is right, the wolf will enter into the home of the target, consume one of their loved ones, and shift into that victim's form, waiting for the target to return and become the perfect dessert to their vicious meal.

A hungersome wolf prefers the prey they find in the First World, but occasionally, one finds their way into the Universe. The resulting carnage inspires many stories whispered in the dark of night to children as a warning—against leaving the trail, against leaving an unprotected loved one alone, and most importantly, a warning to trust your instincts.
